chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I heard a companion of ours asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who dies with men, and there is none with them who is her mahram (close male relative). Can they wash her while she is in her clothes? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then it will be incumbent upon them, but they wash her palms.'

key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: A close male relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُونَهَا: They wash her (ritual bathing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: How do men wash a deceased woman if no mahram is present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of gender mixing in death rituals, establishing that non-mahram men may wash a deceased woman to preserve her modesty (awrah) by keeping her clothed. The specific exception of washing the palms highlights the principle of minimizing exposure to the bare minimum necessary for ritual purity, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the balance between ritual validity and modesty.
